Surah 84: Al-Inshiqaq (The Splitting Asunder)

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿When the sky splits asunder﴾: it cracks open and is torn apart.

The commentary on surah 84, verse 2:

﴿And it hearkens to its Lord and it is right that it should hearken﴾ (and it heard, and obeyed, and answered its Lord by splitting open, and did not refuse, and did not resist).

﴿And it is right that it should hearken﴾ (and it is right for it to hear and obey the command of Allah, since it is created and nurtured by Allah, exalted is He).
And when the earth is stretched out (﴿وَإذا الأرْضُ مُدَّتْ﴾): it is spread out and levelled, with its mountains crumbled flat and everything in it removed.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 84, verse 4:

﴿And it casts out what is within it﴾, and throws out what is in its belly of treasures and the dead,

﴿and empties itself﴾, and becomes utterly empty, until nothing remains within it, as if it were striving to the utmost of its effort to be empty. It is said: "al-karim takarram (the generous one exerted himself in generosity)" when he has reached the utmost of his effort in generosity and has exerted himself beyond what is in his nature.

﴿And it listens to its Lord﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 2], in casting out what is in its belly and emptying itself,

﴿and it is made to obey﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 2], and it is fitting for it to submit and not resist. He omitted the answer (jawab) of "إذا" (idhā, "when"), so that the implied answer (al-muqaddar) may take every possible direction, or because it is understood from its counterpart in the surahs "al-Takwir" and "al-Infitar". Or its answer is what is indicated by ﴿فَمُلَاقِيهِ﴾ ("then you will meet it" [al-Inshiqaq: 6]), meaning: when the sky is split asunder, man will meet his toil (kadh).

"O mankind" (﴿يا أيُّها الإنْسانُ﴾) is an address to the genus, that is, to the human race as a whole.

﴿Indeed, you are toiling toward your Lord with toil﴾: striving toward the meeting with your Lord. The "toil" (kadh, arduous exertion) is death, and what follows it of the state represented by the meeting.

﴿And you will meet it﴾: the pronoun refers to the toil (kadh), which is the exertion of the self in work, and the striving in it until it leaves its mark on the self. The intended meaning is the recompense for the toil: if it is good, then good; if it is evil, then evil. It has also been said that the meeting with the toil is the meeting with a book in which that toil is recorded, as indicated by His saying:

(p-٦٢٠)

Ṭafsīr note: the passage is a short gloss from al-Nasafi's Madarik al-Tanzil on surah 84 (al-Inshiqaq), verse 7.

﴿So as for him who is given his record in his right hand﴾ — i.e., the record of his deeds.

﴿So he will be called to a light account﴾: an easy, gentle reckoning, which means that good deeds will be rewarded and evil deeds overlooked. In a hadith: "Whoever is called to account will be punished." It was said: "Then what of His words: ﴿So he will be called to a light account﴾?" He said: "That is merely the presentation (al-'ard). Whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning will be punished."

﴿And he will return to his family, delighted.﴾ — to his kinsfolk, if they were believers; or to the company of the believers; or to his family in Paradise, namely the wide-eyed houris (al-hur al-'in).

﴿Delighted﴾ — joyful (farihan).

And as for him who is given his record behind his back (﴿وَأمّا مَن أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ وراءَ ظَهْرِهِ﴾), it is said: his right hand will be chained to his neck, and his left hand will be placed behind his back, so that he is given his record with his left hand, from behind his back.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 84, verse 11:

﴿So he will call for destruction (thubur)﴾, meaning he will say: "Woe to me, O destruction!" And "al-thubur" means: ruin, perdition.

﴿وَيَصْلى﴾, "Iraqi (readers) other than ʿAlī" (i.e., read as ﴿وَيُصَلَّى﴾ with the doubled ṣād),

﴿سَعِيرًا﴾ That is: and he will enter Hell (Jahannam).

Surah al-Inshiqaq (84), verse 13 – Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil)

﴿Indeed, he was﴾, in the worldly life,

﴿among his family﴾, with them,

﴿joyful﴾, in disbelief, mocking those who believed in the resurrection. It has been said: he was one who followed his own self, and grazed freely in the pastures of his desires.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 84, verse 14:

﴿Indeed, he thought that he would never return.﴾ "Would never return" means he would never go back to his Lord, denying the resurrection. Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I did not know its meaning until I heard a Bedouin woman say to her daughter: ḥūrī, that is, return (irjiʿī)."

"Yes" (bala) affirms what came after the negation, that he would return. That is: yes, he will surely return.

﴿Indeed, his Lord has always been, concerning him,﴾ and concerning his deeds, ﴿Seeing﴾, nothing hidden from Him. So He will surely bring him back and recompense him for them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 84, verse 16:

﴿So I swear not by the twilight﴾. Then I swear by the whiteness after the redness, or by the redness.

(p-621) ﴿And the night and what it gathers﴾: it gathers and draws together. What is meant is what it gathers of darkness and stars, or what is done in it of tahajjud (voluntary night prayer) and other acts.

﴿And by the moon when it becomes full﴾: it gathers and becomes full, a full moon (badr). It is of the form *iftaʿala* (the reflexive-augmented verbal pattern), from *al-wasq* (the root meaning to gather or load together). The verb here is *اتَّسَقَ*, which is *iftaʿala* (a verb form whose pattern signals reflexive or inceptive action) derived from *الْوَسْقُ*.

ﷺ

**"Surely you will ride (lit. be carried through) stage after stage"** (﴿لَتَرْكَبُنَّ﴾), O human being, taking the word in its generic sense (ʿalā irādat al-jins).

﴿طَبَقًا عَنْ طَبَقٍ﴾: state after state, each one matching its fellow in severity and terror. Al-ṭabaq (lit. "that which matches another"): one says, "This is not a ṭabaq for that," meaning it does not match it. From this comes the word used for a lid or covering, al-ṭabaq. It is also possible that it is the plural of ṭabaqah, meaning a rank or level, from the saying, "He is on ṭabaqāt," meaning: you will indeed ride states after states, which are levels in severity, some higher than others. These are death and what follows of the stations of the Resurrection and its terrors.

The phrase ʿan ṭabaq is in the accusative, either as a qualifier of ṭabaqan, meaning a level exceeding another level, or as a circumstantial state (ḥāl) of the pronoun in latarkabunna, meaning: you will indeed ride levels, passing beyond one another.

Makhūl said: "Every twenty years you will find a matter you were not upon." It is read with the vowel fatḥa on the yāʾ by Makkī, ʿAlī and Ḥamzah. The address is to him (ﷺ), meaning: a level from the levels of the heaven after a level, that is, during the Ascension (al-miʿrāj).
﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe?﴾, meaning: what reason do they have not to believe?!
﴿And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate﴾, meaning they do not humble themselves.

Translation of the passage:

﴿Nay, those who disbelieve deny﴾, [namely, the Resurrection (al-ba'th)] and [the Qur'an].

"And Allah knows best what they conceal" — [meaning] what they gather in their breasts and harbor, of disbelief and denial of the Prophet (ﷺ), or what they gather in their records of evil deeds, and what they store up for themselves of kinds of punishment.
Fa-bashshirhum bi-adhabin alim (So give them tidings of a painful punishment), i.e., inform them with news whose effect will appear upon their skins.

﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: an exception that is disconnected (istithna' munqati', an exception not of the same category as what precedes it).

﴿For them is a reward that is never cut off﴾: not cut off, or not diminished.
